title: Tavarish returns to the fire-damaged Gallardo Spyder that made his name, eight years on
dek: The 2008 Spyder billed as America's cheapest Gallardo lost its twin-turbo kit in a parts trade with HotCars and got a finishing episode in October, but no price has ever been published.

verdict: Impossible to score on money: in eight years Tavarish has not put a public number on what this Spyder cost to buy or fix, as far as we could find. As content it has paid many times over. It anchored more than 70 videos in 2018 [4], fed a parts trade with HotCars in 2026 [6][7] and came back for a finishing episode [1]. As a car, a finished salvage-history Spyder on stock parts is worth roughly $55,000 to $80,000, well under clean examples [10].
body:
## The buy

This is not a new car for Tavarish. The Gallardo he set out to finish on camera in October 2026 is, by every account we could find, the 2008 Gallardo Spyder he picked up years earlier and billed as the cheapest Lamborghini in the country [2][3]. HotCars, which traded parts with him in September 2026, describes his current project as a 2008 Gallardo Spyder [6], the same year and body as the fire-damaged roadster Hooniverse covered in 2018 [3][4].

How and where he bought it has not been reported in anything we could read. Hooniverse called it "the cheapest Lamborghini Gallardo Spyder in the country" but gave no price, seller or auction house [3]. VINwiki's 2018 episode with him describes it as a salvage-title car [5]. We could not open the original purchase video's description [2], so the purchase price stays unknown here.

This is a different car from TheStradman's fire-damaged Gallardo, which he bought back from his own insurer in 2026. The two cars share a model and a misfortune, and nothing else.

## The damage

When Tavarish got it, the Spyder was fire damaged and not drivable, according to HotCars' later summary of his collection [11]. It was not stock either. A previous owner had fitted a twin-turbo kit to the V10, and Hooniverse listed a "busted" twin-turbo setup, a "wonky" transmission and "many other issues" on top of the fire [3]. The work it needed ran to paint and body, new plumbing and electrical work and major engine work [3]. VINwiki framed the project as one critics said could not be done [5].

## The work and the parts

The build has two lives. The first ran through 2018 and took more than 70 videos [4]. By late 2018 the engine ran, the twin-turbo system worked and a manual gearbox was in [4], and Hooniverse declared the car finished in November of that year [3]. That was about nine months after the saga began, by Hooniverse's count [3].

The second life is the 2026 return. In September, HotCars published an episode of its own salvage Gallardo build in which it traded its stock Gallardo engine for "Tavarish's twin turbo setup" [7]. HotCars wrote that Tavarish needed stock, hard-to-find factory parts from its car for his Spyder [6]. In short, the twin-turbo hardware that defined the first build appears to have left the car, and factory parts went the other way. Neither side published a price for the trade.

Short clips syndicated on MSN around the finishing episode show Tavarish fixing the Spyder's clutch without replacing it [8], and detailing an LP 570-style front bumper and rear cowl for the car [9]. The finishing episode itself went up on October 31, 2026 [1]. We could not read its full description, so the parts list below is limited to what the coverage names. Not one part comes with a price.

## The money

No dollar figure for this car has been published in anything we could read: not the purchase price, not the parts, not the value of the engine-for-turbos trade with HotCars [3][6][7]. Our cost table is therefore empty except for its notes. Tavarish's own labor, spread over two rounds of work eight years apart, is not counted.

What we can do is price the result. Clean 2008 Gallardo Spyders have recently sold for $84,700 to $111,222 in classic.com's records, with most around $85,000 to $96,000 [10]. Those cars have clean titles and factory drivetrains. Tavarish's has a salvage history from a fire [5], a non-original body kit and a powertrain that has been modified, unmodified and swapped. A salvage or rebuilt title usually takes 20% to 40% off a car's value, and buyers of fire cars tend to sit at the bottom of that range. On that basis we put the finished Spyder at about $55,000 to $80,000; its fame as a YouTube car could lift that at a no-reserve auction.

## What's next

The finishing episode's title says Tavarish is setting out to "prove everyone wrong" [1]. Whether the car is fully done, registered and driving, or whether more episodes follow, is not clear from what we could read. The questions worth answering are whether the Spyder keeps the stock HotCars engine, whether he will finally say what the car has cost, and whether it stays in his collection or goes up for sale. We will update the file if he does.
